original_forecast: If only the requested first arm esterifies, its remaining acid demand should be lower than the unactivated feed control. The titration-derived difference should be checked against the pre-workup ester inventory.

original_criteria.criterion: Compare delivered hydroxide equivalents and separately inspect the acid and ester pools before dilution.
Check whether dilution or titration causes further hydrolysis; do not interpret that extra reaction as original conversion.

original_limitations: The named transformation is a teaching model; aqueous speciation ownership and base-induced ester hydrolysis can compromise a simple endpoint assay.

named_model_boundaries.what: a mixed solvent that is mostly organic (water is 33% of the liquid): the shipped activity models assume water as the solvent, and in this dielectric environment their equilibrium constants do not apply, so ionic speciation here is reported uncharacterised

scope: Original conditional requested ideal-mixture teaching model only; K4 and no reaction heat/temperature/activity dependence remain explicit. No claim about actual esterification rate, catalyst sufficiency, true thermodynamic equilibrium or empirical assay calibration.

Pure-organic initial request yields uncharacterised ionic state honestly; original assay occurs only after100mLwater addition with actual solved pH. The one mostly-organic warning does not establish failed original chemistry or authority for physical mixed-solvent acid/base values.

No extra ester hydrolysis is observed across saved dilution/titration commands, and source dose closure advances no time. This is a requested-only model observation, not proof of chemical inertness during a real time-consuming titration.
